# 3 Maccabees Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** The Elephants Miraculously Restrained

---

**1** Hermon had prepared the elephants and was getting ready to drive them into the hippodrome at dawn.

**2** But the Lord sent a deep and pleasant sleep upon the king, and in this way the Lord defeated his lawless scheme and frustrated his stubborn will.

**3** The king slept soundly right through until late morning; and when he finally woke up from his heavy sleep, he could not remember a thing.

**4** He asked the servants around him why he had slept so late, since it was always his habit to deal with affairs of state from early in the morning.

**5** When they explained what had happened, he gave orders for the Jews to be brought in immediately and made no mention whatsoever of the elephants.

**6** The court officials, and especially the king's Friends, were amazed that such a heavy sleep had come over the king, and they praised God for delivering the Jews.

**7** When the Jews heard that the king's plan had changed, they praised their guardian God and prayed again for his protection, while the bolder among them took great courage.

**8** Meanwhile, Hermon was completely thrown by the sudden reversal and went to report to the king, saying: My Lord the King, we are prepared and ready to carry out your command whenever you give the word.

**9** But the king looked at him with a terrifying expression and said: If your own parents or children were here, I would have fed them to the wild beasts, as recompense for those who have plotted against and dishonored me.

**10** Hermon, receiving this unexpected and dangerous rebuke, was greatly distressed and his face fell.

**11** The Friends gradually steered the king's attention to other matters and managed to calm his fury.

**12** Once again the same deep, persistent sleep settled over the king.

**13** Once again the Jews were saved from complete destruction.

**14** After the king came to himself again, still troubled, he said: What is this? Why have you disturbed me? I gave no command in this matter.

**15** But when the Friends, the chief stewards and managers of affairs, reminded him, he flew into a sudden rage and ordered the Jews to be brought to the hippodrome the very next morning.

**16** Those in charge of the prisoners went away in great confusion and disorder; returning to the hippodrome, they were overcome with pity at the sight of the imprisoned Jews.

**17** Hermon was among them, and he was the one responsible for the whole situation. He mixed wine and frankincense and got the five hundred elephants thoroughly drunk, then drove them forward as the king had commanded.

**18** But a man named Eleazar, prominent among the Jewish priests, raised his voice and called out to the Lord in prayer:

**19** O great King, Most High God, Almighty, who governs all creation with mercy, look upon the descendants of Abraham, upon the children of the consecrated Jacob, upon your holy inheritance, O Father, who are being unjustly put to death as foreigners in a foreign land.

**20** You drove Egypt and Pharaoh away with plague after plague when they arrogantly oppressed our holy fathers.

**21** You are the Lord of lords, the Governor of all creation; look upon us now.

**22** Have mercy on us in our bitter distress, and let your mercy rescue us from this evil.

**23** Hear our prayer and turn aside the wickedness being done against us.

**24** Shatter the power of arrogance; let the One who saved Abraham from the furnace of the Chaldeans also save us now.

**25** As you showed mercy to Daniel in the lions' den, and to the three holy youths Ananias, Azariah, and Mishael, so show mercy to us as well.
